hook: SCP-5657 is read over the shoulder of someone browsing the files, and that someone keeps skipping ahead and ordering things deleted. Pay attention to who is asking and why. Expect a brutal motel fight with gunfire, crushed skulls and a woman beaten nearly to death, plus an interviewer who insinuates she once sold physical intimacy.
whyItMatters:
The entry is a strong example of the framing device carrying the plot: the order in which documents open, and which ones get purged, is controlled by a character inside the story. The glitching system messages make the security AI feel like a participant rather than a backdrop.

At its center is a vivid character, a brash empath turned talk-show host whose description of what emotions feel like through touch is some of the most memorable writing in the file.
thingsToNotice:
The visitor is a Smiling Man, one of the empty human mimics hunting Nicki, and its questions are about how she survived so its kind can use her. The opening test looks like it fails mid-phrase and the AI looks overwritten, and the interloper reveals that Adelard sold her out after they took his colleague Wills. Then its hand passes through her neck: Nicki is a hologram, she was moved out twenty minutes earlier, and the curiosity that kept it reading files was an emotion she pushed into it with that first touch. EVAS admits it was acting, and the cell built to keep the Smiling Men out now holds one in.

The interviews set this up. Nicki explains that ordinary people are too full for her to project feelings into, but an empty being catches like dry kindling, which is how she made her attacker cry and how she now traps this one. Her final smile, aimed at a creature that once thought smiling was only lip movement, closes the loop as she tells it that it is now SCP-5657.
